mission.display_title: State and apply the CLT for an iid sequence

mission.learning_objective: State and apply the central limit theorem for a sequence of independent, identically distributed random variables.
mission.concept_focus: iid sequence → mean/variance conditions (CMP) → standardised sample mean → Normal limit → refuse Normal-everywhere theatre.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.5.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) State the CLT for an iid sequence in one or two sentences (conditions + conclusion). (2) What random quantity is becoming approximately Normal? (3) Name one reason 'the Normal is common' is not the same as stating the CLT.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Under CMP conditions (iid; finite mean/variance as stated), the standardised sample mean (or sum) converges in distribution to Normal as n increases. Knowing the Normal shape is not the same as stating this limit theorem for iid sequences.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.5.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A colleague says 'we already use the Normal all the time, so the CLT is just common sense.' Refuse in one sentence and restate what today's LO adds.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse: casual Normal use is not the CLT. Today's skill is stating and applying the theorem for iid sequences under CMP conditions (standardised means → Normal).
